chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

It was said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Does your Lord have the power to place the world in an egg, without making the world smaller or the egg bigger?' He answered: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be described by means of limits. However, what you have asked is impossible.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine omnipotence and logical impossibility in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* clarifies the Shia doctrine of divine omnipotence by distinguishing between absolute power (*Qudrah Mutlaqah*) and logical impossibility (*Maqdur al-Mumtani*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserts that God’s inability to perform a contradictory act, such as placing the vast universe inside a small egg without altering either, stems from the inherent nature of the elements rather than any deficiency in God’s power. This aligns with the principle that God does not do what is impossible by definition, preserving His perfection while acknowledging logical constraints.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 9. Muhammad ibn `Ali Majilwayh (RA) said, on the authority of his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Madani, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of `Umar ibn Udhaynah, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

The Commander of the Faithful (AS) was asked: “Does Your Lord have the power to place the Earth in an egg, without making the Earth smaller or the egg any bigger?” He answered, “Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be described by means of limits. However, what you have asked is impossible.”
